owner_to_confirm_before_push: Each wheel's reading is shown to the customer ('we'll show you the numbers'). The live page already says so; confirm it is what staff do. If you hand out a printout, say 'printout' instead.

The NE balancer can flag a slightly bent wheel (rim runout) and gives match-mount guidance. Lines that depend on it: hero subheading ('look for … a slightly bent wheel'), comparison row 'A slightly bent wheel' ('Can flag one'), how_3 and comparison row 5 ('show you the numbers'), FAQ 8 and the LT bullet ('fits our machine'). If it can't, set cmp_3 col_a to 'Depends on the machine' and how_3_text to 'We road force test and balance each wheel and match mount any tire that needs it.'
Which large tires the NE machine fits (the page asks customers to give their tire size when booking; it doesn't promise 35 or 37 inch).
The $15 per tire road force upgrade applies to any job booked at Edmonton Trail NE, per commit 8814084. The page says 'a tire installation or another job'.
The $35 per wheel price applies to tires bought anywhere (FAQ 12 and price row 1 say so).
Shop location wording 'on Edmonton Trail NE between 16 Ave and McKnight Boulevard' (location note). True, but 3928 sits around 39–40 Ave NE, so 'near 40 Ave NE' would be more exact once confirmed.

NE hours. The brief says Mon-Sat 9:30-5:30 and Sun 10:00-3:30; the live store_hours metaobject says Mon-Thu and Sat 9-6, Fri 9-1 and 2:30-5, Sun 10-4. The page shows no hours (location_card_show_hours is false) and only says 'open seven days a week', which is true under both. Fix the metaobject first, then switch location_card_show_hours on.

Studded tires: left off the page on purpose. Hunter's current manual says not to use the load roller on studded tires; the NE machine's brand is unverified. Once staff confirm their rule, add the ready-made FAQ below.
The machine's brand. The page names Hunter only as the source of the term and the published limits; it never says Prince uses a Hunter.

Drip pricing (Competition Act s.74.01(1.1)): confirm the $35 per wheel covers the balance, the load test, match mounting with the remount and rebalance, and the weights, with no shop-supplies or disposal fee added, and that any TPMS service-kit charge is optional. If any fixed fee applies, it must go into the shown price everywhere (title tag, price rows, schema offers, FAQ 2, GBP).
The +$15 upgrade applies to a seasonal changeover too (GBP post 4 and the page's 'another job at Edmonton Trail NE').

The '⭐ 4.9 / 5 on Google' trust-strip text is hardcoded in pt-calgary-service. On an NE-only page readers will read it as the NE profile's rating. Check the NE profile; if the 4.9 is the 42 Ave SW profile, this page needs a different figure or '(42 Ave SW)'.

The new line 'Prince Tires is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hunter Engineering' (panel_what). True whatever brand the NE machine is, but if Prince gets listed on Hunter's locator, keep it as 'not endorsed by'.

Two sources still unverified in a real browser (both return 403 to scripted fetches): the Brake & Front End article (the page now says 'especially useful on very low-profile tires', no '45-series' quote) and the Tesla Model Y manual page (125 N; en-cn locale link, en-us and en-ca also 403 to scripts). Open both in a browser before push; swap the Tesla link to en-us if it shows the same procedure.

The built template's order is ['main'] only. Pushing it removes the two live pt-tire-explainer sections (explainer-what, explainer-signs). Their content has moved into panels; this also removes the live, unsourced line 'Most passenger tires are fine under about 15 to 20 lb'. Confirm that's intended.

Hero/location-card/closing CTA label changed from 'Book road force balancing' to 'Request road force balancing'. It is also the data-pt-label analytics value: update any GTM trigger that matches the old label.

Shared-section fallbacks changed for every page using pt-calgary-service: trust_2 '✓ Same-day available' → '✓ Request a time online', cta_bottom_text 'Join hundreds of Calgary drivers who trust Prince Tires.' → 'Pick a time online and we’ll confirm it with you, or give us a call.' ready_to_add_faq_once_confirmed.question: Can you road force balance studded tires?
ready_to_add_faq_once_confirmed.answer_if_no: No. The load roller isn't meant for studded tires, so studded winter sets get a standard balance ($20 per wheel at both shops). If a studded set shakes after a balance, call (825) 395-4024 and we'll talk through what else it could be.
